q.title: Divorce questionnaire
q.subtitle: Answer a few simple questions and we will prepare your filing summary.

state.question: Which state will you file in?

petitionerName.question: What is your full legal name?

respondentName.question: What is your spouse’s full legal name?

county.question: Which county will you file in?

residency.question: Has at least one spouse lived in the filing state for 6 months or more?

uncontested.question: Do both spouses agree to the divorce and all of its terms?

minorChildren.question: Do you have any minor children together?

propertySplit.question: Have you already agreed on how to divide all property and debts?

ineligible.title: Not eligible for the $30 uncontested path
ineligible.lead: Based on your answers, this service can’t prepare your paperwork. Here’s why:

reasons.NON_RESIDENT: The filing state must be Texas or Oklahoma.
reasons.NO_RESIDENCY_DURATION: At least one spouse must have lived in the filing state for 6 months or more.
reasons.CONTESTED: Both spouses must agree to the divorce and all of its terms.
reasons.MINOR_CHILDREN: This path is only for couples with no minor children together.
reasons.PROPERTY_DISPUTE: You must agree on the division of all property and debts first.

organizer.title: Filing organizer
organizer.disclaimer: DOGS is not a law firm and this summary is not legal advice. Verify all forms and requirements with your county clerk or a licensed attorney before filing.

tx_petition.title: File the Original Petition for Divorce
tx_petition.detail: File with the district clerk in your county and pay the filing fee. Keep a stamped copy.

tx_service.title: Serve your spouse — or file a Waiver of Service
tx_service.detail: If your spouse signs a Waiver of Service after the petition is filed, you can skip formal service.

tx_waiting.title: Wait out the 60-day waiting period
tx_waiting.detail: Texas requires at least 60 days between filing and the final decree, except in cases involving family violence.

tx_decree.title: Complete the Agreed Final Decree of Divorce
tx_decree.detail: Fill in every section, have both spouses sign, and bring it to your prove-up hearing.

ok_petition.title: File the Petition for Dissolution of Marriage
ok_petition.detail: File with the court clerk in your county and pay the filing fee. Keep a stamped copy.

ok_appearance.title: File an Entry of Appearance and Waiver
ok_appearance.detail: Your spouse signs this to waive formal service and consent to the court’s jurisdiction.

ok_waiting.title: Check for a local waiting period
ok_waiting.detail: Oklahoma has no mandatory waiting period for divorces without minor children, but confirm with your county clerk.

ok_decree.title: Complete the Decree of Dissolution of Marriage
ok_decree.detail: Fill in every section, have both spouses sign, and present it to the judge.

file_decree.title: File the decree and get certified copies
file_decree.detail: After the judge signs, file the decree with the clerk and get certified copies for your records.
